reconcile.note: Gill treats 7:14's sanctification as marital status, not salvation, so Paul's doubt in 7:16 doesn't conflict with Acts 16:31, which he ties to the household's own faith.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible juxtaposes Acts 16:31's household salvation promise with Paul's own admission in 1 Corinthians 7:16 that a spouse cannot know whether she will save her husband, reading them as incompatible answers.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.
sides.verseText: They said, \"Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.\"

sides.snippet: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
sides.verseText: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
